title: Hosted Endpoint Jurisdiction Locker and Evidence Synthesis Wizard
creator: Asha Nguyen
description:
Problem: Customers running the Hosted API need a frictionless way to assert and lock the jurisdictions where their request data, cached state, and derived artifacts may be stored, while automatically producing legally consumable evidence bundles for audits. Current controls are fragmented (region filters + adhoc logs) and do not surface retention windows or proof artifacts for a tenant-level attestation.

Scope: Build a 'Jurisdiction Locker' in the Hosted control plane that lets tenants: (1) declare one or more jurisdiction constraints (country/region/sovereignty level), (2) pin endpoints to a chosen primary jurisdiction with fallback rules, (3) specify retention policies per endpoint, and (4) generate an evidence bundle (signed, time-stamped manifest + telemetry + region routing proof + retention proof) for compliance teams. This ticket covers PM requirements, acceptance criteria, UI wizard flows, API contract stub, and the evidence synthesis orchestration. Engineering work (runtime routing, datastore tagging, and signing) is tracked in ENG tickets listed in dependencies.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include on-prem agents or Dedicated capacity controls. It does not change low-level kernel selection or batching behavior. It does not attempt to certify country-level legal compliance (legal sign-off is required before customer-facing verbiage).
acceptance_criteria: Tenant can create a 'Jurisdiction Locker' for a hosted endpoint and choose from a list of allowed jurisdictions (list populated from regulatory taxonomy).
Locker UI exposes an explicit 'Pin to jurisdiction' action and a separate 'Fallback topology' selector (same-region, geo-nearest within allowed, operator-queue).
Per-endpoint retention windows (range selection and presets: 7d, 30d, 90d, custom) are attachable to lockers and appear in the evidence bundle metadata.

Evidence bundle generation: single-click export that includes: signed manifest (locker settings, timestamps, tenant ID), routing traces for a sample time window, retention enforcement events, and a signed checksum index. Bundle format is ZIP+JSON and stored in tenant audit logs with a signed pointer in control plane UI.

API: New REST endpoints created under /v1/tenants/{tid}/lockers for CRUD and /v1/tenants/{tid}/lockers/{lid}/evidence to generate/download bundles. End-to-end integration tests for these endpoints exist in the API test suite.
Telemetry: each pinned routing decision emits route.reason and route.region tags; retention enforcement emits retention.applied and retention.expiry tags which feed Console dashboards.
Legal: Documentation copy for the locker UI and the evidence semantics is approved by Legal (approval recorded in ticket comments).
Rollout: Feature gated behind 'residency-locker' feature flag and available in staged form for 5 pilot tenants before general availability.
api_contract:
Summary: POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/lockers { name, jurisdictions: [ISO-3166 codes], pin_mode: ENUM(primary|soft|none), fallback_policy: ENUM(same-region|geo-nearest|operator-queue), retention: {preset|days|until_date}, notes }
GET returns locker object with status and applied routes. POST /.../evidence?from=XXX&to=YYY triggers async evidence bundle creation and returns job id. Job status endpoints and signed download URL returned on completion.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Alpha behind feature flag - internal Redwood tenants + infra canaries
Week 2: Invite 5 pilot customers (legal/data owners signed NDAs) - collect feedback on UI and bundle artifacts
Week 3: Iterate on evidence format and add signer HSM key rotation support
Week 4: Expand to GA behind opt-in release, monitor Console SLOs and evidence generation latency

Fallback/Rollback: toggle 'residency-locker' feature flag to disable new routing logic and fall back to existing region matching; evidence bundles remain downloadable but new bundle generation disabled.
test_plan: Unit tests for locker CRUD, validation for jurisdiction lists and retention presets.
Integration tests verifying routing tags when pin_mode=primary and when fallback policy selected.
E2E tests that generate an evidence bundle and validate structure + signed checksum.
Load test: generate 1k evidence bundles in 1 hour in staging to measure control-plane CPU and storage impact.
Security test: signed bundle verification and HSM key rotation scenario tested with Security team.
engineering_notes: Trade-offs discussed on 2025-02-20: embedding route proofs in the bundle (detailed packet traces) vs summarized route assertions (latency/cost tradeoff). Decided to include detailed routing trace for first release; sampling window will be configurable.
KV cache tagging: runtime must attach 'locker_id' and 'jurisdiction' tags to cached prefixes so eviction/replication can respect jurisdiction constraints. ENG-92012 will implement tagging layer.
Signing: evidence bundle will be signed using a tenant-scoped certificate stored in KMS; Security proposes UX that surfaces signing key rotation schedule.
Storage: evidence bundles stored in tenant audit bucket (retention of bundles follows tenant retention policy). Consider cost cap for very frequent bundle generation.
cross_team_tasks: Legal: approve evidence bundle schema and standard wording for UI.
Security: finalize signing algorithm and KMS integration pattern.
Engineering (runtime): ensure tags emitted and route proofs collected; implement fallback operators.
Console: build 'Locker' creation wizard and evidence download flow.
Support: update runbooks and add KB article template for tenant requests.
